title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
oneLinerQuestion: Build a structure that supports adding words and searching with wildcard dots.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Design Add and Search Words Data Structure (WordDictionary) problem requires supporting two operations: adding words and searching words where a '.' character can match any letter. While standard Trie search traverses a deterministic single path for exact characters, encountering a wildcard '.' means the next character could match any existing child branch. To handle this, we augment standard Trie traversal with Depth-First Search (DFS) backtracking: when an alphabetical character is met, we follow its direct child link deterministically; when a '.' is encountered, we branch into all existing children at the current node level, returning true if any branch successfully matches the remaining suffix.

- Step 1: Node & Class Setup — We define a `TrieNode` containing a `children` map/dictionary (storing lowercase letter mappings) and an `isWord = false` terminal boolean flag. The `WordDictionary` constructor initializes `this.root = new TrieNode()`.

- Step 2: Implementing addWord(word) — Standard Trie insertion: iterate character by character starting from `curr = this.root`. If `!curr.children[char]`, instantiate a new `TrieNode`. Move `curr` to the child node. After inserting all characters, mark the terminal node with `curr.isWord = true`.

- Step 3: DFS Helper Definition for search(word) — We implement a recursive helper `dfs(index, node)` that evaluates the search query from character position `index` starting at the given Trie `node`.

- Step 4: Deterministic Character Branching — If `word[index]` is an alphabetical character: check if `node.children[word[index]]` exists. If it does not, return `false`. If it exists, advance to that child by returning `dfs(index + 1, node.children[word[index]])`.

- Step 5: Wildcard '.' Backtracking Branching — If `word[index] === '.'`: iterate through all non-null child nodes present in `Object.values(node.children)`. For each child, recursively execute `dfs(index + 1, child)`. If any child branch returns `true`, immediately propagate `return true`. If all branches are exhausted without a match, return `false`.

- Step 6: Base Case & Method Trigger — The base case triggers when `index === word.length`, where we return `node.isWord` to ensure a complete word terminates at this point. The public method initiates the search via `return dfs(0, this.root)`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: `addWord` runs in O(L) time where L is the length of the word; `search` runs in O(L) for words without wildcards and up to O(26^L) in the worst case if every character is '.' across a dense dictionary. Space Complexity: O(M * L) auxiliary space for storing M words of average length L in the Trie, with O(L) auxiliary stack depth during DFS recursion.
pseudoCode:
CLASS WordDictionary:
    CONSTRUCTOR(): root = NEW TrieNode()
    FUNCTION addWord(word):
        curr = root
        FOR c IN word DO:
            IF c NOT IN curr.children THEN curr.children[c] = NEW TrieNode()
            curr = curr.children[c]
        END FOR
        curr.isWord = True
    FUNCTION search(word):
        FUNCTION dfs(j, root):
            curr = root
            FOR i FROM j TO LENGTH(word) - 1 DO:
                c = word[i]
                IF c == '.' THEN:
                    FOR child IN curr.children.values() DO:
                        IF dfs(i + 1, child) THEN RETURN True
                    END FOR
                    RETURN False
                ELSE:
                    IF c NOT IN curr.children THEN RETURN False
                    curr = curr.children[c]
            END FOR
            RETURN curr.isWord
        END FUNCTION
        RETURN dfs(0, root)
END CLASS
